resources.string: The limit may not have reset. Switch the bike on (or unlock it) and tap %1$d to restore it.
Can’t reach your bike yet. Switch it on, close the ENGWE app and stay near it. The app keeps trying.
Not turned off: the bike wasn’t reporting that it was on.
Not turned on: the bike wasn’t reporting that it was off.
Not turned off: the bike wasn’t reading 0\u00A0km/h. Stop, then tap the app’s power button again.
Not turned on: the bike wasn’t connected. Tap the app’s power button again once it’s connected.
Not turned off: the bike wasn’t connected. Tap the app’s power button again once it’s connected.
Not turned on: another change was still being sent. Tap the app’s power button again.
Not turned off: another change was still being sent. Tap the app’s power button again.
Not turned on yet. Tap the app’s power button to send it.
Not turned off yet. Tap the app’s power button to send it.
The bike didn’t confirm turning on. Try again, switch it on at its display, or unlock it in the ENGWE app.
The bike didn’t confirm turning off. Try again, or switch it off at its display.
Your bike reports the model identity %1$s. It matches a model the project tested.
Your bike reports the model identity %1$s. The project hasn’t tested this model.

The app can’t read the bike’s IoT firmware. Verified means tested with IoT firmware %1$s on one bike: check yours in the ENGWE app. On other firmware a change might behave differently, including not resetting when the bike turns off: tap %2$d and report it.
The app can’t read the bike’s IoT firmware: check it in the ENGWE app and add it to your report.
Changes may behave differently on this model and might not reset when the bike turns off: tap %1$d to restore. Its readings may be wrong.

A model the project hasn’t tested is verified after at least two independent reports (different riders and bikes), each with a session log showing the bike’s confirmations and saying that, with 32\u00A0km/h set, assistance stopped within 2\u00A0km/h of it. Ride only where it is legal. COMPATIBILITY.md in the project’s repository has the details.
Bike switched on · in the project’s tests, the limit started at %1$d\u00A0km/h
No speed set by this app yet
In the project’s tests, a speed set here lasted until the bike was switched off.
In the project’s tests, turning the bike off and on in this app reset the limit to %1$d\u00A0km/h too, as switching it off and on at the display does.
It may not reset when the bike turns off: tap %1$d to restore.
Not known whether a speed resets when this bike turns off. Tap %1$d to restore.
Not confirmed. Tap %1$d to try again.
Bike restarted. In the project’s tests, this set the limit back to %1$d\u00A0km/h.
The bike reported switching off and on. The limit may not be back to %1$d\u00A0km/h: tap %1$d to restore.
The bike reported switching off and on · re-applying %1$d\u00A0km/h…
The bike reported switching off and on. Tap %1$d to be sure the limit is %1$d\u00A0km/h.
%1$d\u00A0km/h not sent: the bike wasn’t reporting that it was on. Switch it on, wait a moment and tap %1$d again.
%1$d\u00A0km/h not sent: the bike wasn’t connected. Tap %1$d again once it’s connected.
%1$d\u00A0km/h not sent: another change was still being sent. Tap %1$d again.
%1$d\u00A0km/h not sent yet. Tap %1$d to set it.
Marked speeds are above %1$d\u00A0km/h, the EU limit for e-bikes. Use them only where it is legal, for example on private land, at your own risk.
The bike can’t report its limit: the card shows only what the app sent and whether the bike confirmed it.
After the app reconnects or opens again, a speed set earlier may still hold even if none is marked. Tap %1$d to be sure.
Set again after restarts and reconnections, at most once a minute, while the app is open
Set again each time the app connects to the bike, while the app is open. After you switch the bike off and on, tap the speed again.
The bike reported switching off and on · setting assist %1$d again…
Assist %1$d · set again on connecting, confirmed by the bike
Assist %1$d · set again after the bike switched on, confirmed by the bike
Assist %1$d not confirmed. Tap %1$d to try again.
The app shows this model’s assist level but can’t set it.
Not set: the bike wasn’t reporting that it was on. Tap a level to try again.
Not set: the bike wasn’t connected. Tap a level to try again.
Not set: another change was still being sent. Tap a level to try again.
Not set yet. Tap a level to set it.
Asks the bike to change its assist level. A level shows as set only once the bike confirms the command and its status shows the new level.
Once the bike is checked, the card shows its assist level and, where the app can set it, its levels.
Set again after restarts and reconnections, at most once a minute, while the app is open, and only while the bike reads 0\u00A0km/h. A level changed on the bike’s display isn’t kept.
Set again once each time the app connects to the bike, while the app is open, and only while the bike reads 0\u00A0km/h. A level changed on the bike’s display isn’t kept.
Not confirmed. Tap to try again.
Not switched: the bike wasn’t reporting that it was on. Tap to try again.
Not switched: the bike wasn’t connected. Tap to try again.
Not switched: another change was still being sent. Tap to try again.
Not switched yet. Tap to switch the lights.
In the EU, e-bikes must stop assisting at %2$d\u00A0km/h. Use %1$d\u00A0km/h only where it is legal, for example on private land. You ride at your own risk.

In the EU, e-bikes must stop assisting at %2$d\u00A0km/h. %1$d\u00A0km/h is far above that: braking distances get much longer, and the motor, brakes and tyres are under much more stress. Use %1$d\u00A0km/h only where it is legal, for example on private land. You ride at your own risk.
With “Keep this speed” on, the app sets %1$d\u00A0km/h again after each restart or reconnection (at most once a minute), while the app is open.
With “Keep this speed” on, the app sets %1$d\u00A0km/h again each time it connects to the bike, while the app is open. After you switch the bike off and on, it doesn’t.
